title: fix(sdk): preserve streamed error semantics
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Ignore null error fields on successful stream events.
- Reject terminal finish_reason=error even without an error object.
- Preserve explicit error statuses and machine-readable codes; unknown failures remain 502.
- Adds regression coverage for null errors, terminal failures, policy/rate-limit errors, and invalid statuses. SDK tests and typecheck pass.

gist.headline: Streams keep their sting
gist.blurb: The SDK now knows the difference between a harmless empty error field and a stream that actually went sideways. Real failures arrive with their useful status codes intact, rather than wearing a generic 502 costume.
gist.summary: Fixed SDK streaming error handling so successful events with null error fields continue normally, terminal finish_reason=error events reject even without an error object, and explicit policy or rate-limit statuses and machine-readable codes are preserved.
gist.impact: Developers consuming streamed responses get reliable failures: null errors no longer interrupt healthy streams, while terminal, policy, and rate-limit failures expose their actual status and code instead of collapsing into an unknown 502.
gist.visual_concept: Polli acts as a careful streamkeeper at a cozy terminal, using a small sieve to let harmless null bubbles flow through while catching genuine red error leaves labeled with clear status codes. A code-plant and softly glowing stream of API packets make the distinction between healthy events and terminal failures visible.
